title: Google 3.38 亿美元英国开发者和解案开放申领
content:
Google’s $338m UK developer settlement opens for claims – Mobilegamer.biz
Skip to content
Any UK developer that has sold apps, games, subscriptions or in-app content through Google Play since August 2018 is now eligible for a share of a $338m (£260m) settlement with Google.
More than 10,000 UK businesses are thought to be eligible, and developers can check their provisional award and claim for free through the
official claims website
. The claims period runs from today (November 24) until March 24, 2027.
The settlement stems from a collective action brought by Professor Barry Rodger of Strathclyde University Law School, which alleged that Google’s Play Store commissions of up to 30% were excessive and broke competition law. Google settled without admitting liability, and the Competition Appeal Tribunal approved the deal on September 16, finding its terms just and reasonable.
According to Rodger’s legal team, it’s the largest payout for members of a collective action the Tribunal has ever approved.
Payments are based on Google’s records of each developer’s Play Store sales and the commission they paid between August 22, 2018 and July 31, 2026. Developers whose apps made $9,750 (£7,500) or less on the Play Store during that period are guaranteed a minimum of $260 (£200), even if their proportionate share would have been lower. The biggest developers could receive millions.
Apps that were free to download are also eligible, as long as they sold subscriptions or in-app content and the developer didn’t opt out of the claim.
As the case was brought on an opt-out basis, many eligible developers may not know about it. Invitations to claim have been emailed to the addresses linked to developers’ Google Play accounts, but those who haven’t received one can still check their eligibility on the claims website.
“If an email about a Google settlement has landed in your inbox, it isn’t spam,” said Rodger. “After more than two years of work, compensation is now ready for the UK businesses that sold apps and digital content on the Google Play Store, from one-person studios working at their kitchen tables to established games companies.”
Once the claims period closes, the Tribunal will review how the settlement is distributed before any payments are made.
The case is separate from the
collective claim brought by Liz Coll
on behalf of UK consumers, which is currently going through trial.
